summary: In Greek mythology, Thoön (Ancient Greek Θόων) is a Homeric warrior name borne by several Trojans and allies. This atlas node is the Trojan whom Agamemnon slays in his Book 11 aristeia (Iliad 11.422), distinct from the Phaenopid twin killed by Diomedes and from other namesakes on the shared Wikipedia page.
etymology: Thóōn is a short Homeric fighting name; nodes are fixed by killer, patronymic, or book context rather than by the bare name.

sections.heading: Agamemnon's victim
paragraphs: In Iliad 11 Agamemnon, raging among the Trojan press after Deïopites, slays Thoön and Ennomus before turning on Chersidamas. The poem gives this Thoön no patronymic — only the king's spear and the roll of the slain.
Later lists and Ovid's Ulysses speech sometimes redistribute Thoön-kills among other Achaeans; the atlas keeps thoon-trojan as Agamemnon's Homeric target, not Odysseus' or Antilochus'.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: Not Thoön son of Phaenops, twin of Xanthus, slain by Diomedes (thoon-phaenopid); not the Trojan Antilochus kills at the Achaean wall; not the Giant Thoas/Thoon (thoas-giant); not the Lycian, Phaeacian, Dionysiac, or Icariad namesakes gathered on Wikipedia's disambiguation page.
